The region enclosed by the curve $y=(x-1)^{4}$ and the horizontal line $y=1$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $y=1.$ Find the volume $V$ of the resulting solid. Do not round the answer.

$V=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curve and the line by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{4} & =1 \\ x-1 & =\pm 1 \\ x & =0,2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the limits of integration are from $x=0$ to $x=2$ along the $x$-axis. 

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222139/assets/2a2e4be26d18e408bf6e4580c72ec2f3c08eed1750d38e0716f06a32d3c03e7c.png)

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=(x-1)^{4},$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=1.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our volume is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}{[\,1-(x-1)^{4}\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}(1-2(x-1)^{4}+(x-1)^{8})\,\,\text{d}x \\  & =\pi {(x-\frac{2}{5}(x-1)^{5}+\frac{1}{9}(x-1)^{9}\text{ })|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\pi ([2-\frac{2}{5}(1)^{5}+\frac{1}{9}(1)^{9}\text{ }]-[0-\frac{2}{5}(-1)^{5}+\frac{1}{9}(-1)^{9}\text{ }]) \\  & =\frac{64\pi }{45}.\end{aligned}
$$
